result.markdown: --- title: "Visualizing Soccer Data" description: "Exploring Argentina vs. Saudi Arabia match via Data viz using Python " date: "2026-05-25" categories: [Python, EDA, Soccer, Data, Visualization, StatsBomb] format: html: code-fold: true code-tools: true jupyter: python3 --- ## Overview I had used R, ggplot2, ggsoccer and other R packages to build visualizations for my 2022 world cup microsite showcasing Argentina's progress In this blog post, I'm using Python to explore building a few different set of visualizations for the Argentina vs. Saudi Arabia game ## Tools Used - **Languages:** Python - **IDE:** Positron - **Packages:** quarto, pandas, numpy, mplsoccer ## Python Imports ::: {#0492e925 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import matplotlib.patches as mpatches from mplsoccer import Pitch, VerticalPitch, Sbopen import pandas as pd import numpy as np from adjustText import adjust_text ``` ::: ## Finding the match id's for Argentina's games ::: {#e82e918c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # https://mplsoccer.readthedocs.io/en/latest/gallery/statsbomb/plot_statsbomb_data.html#match-data parser = Sbopen() # 2022 World Cup matches = parser.match(competition_id=43, season_id=106) TEAM = "Argentina" team_matches = matches[ (matches['home_team_name'] == TEAM) | (matches['away_team_name'] == TEAM) ] print(team_matches[['match_id', 'home_team_name', 'away_team_name', 'match_date']].to_string()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` match_id home_team_name away_team_name match_date 24 3869321 Netherlands Argentina 2022-12-09 27 3869685 Argentina France 2022-12-18 30 3869151 Argentina Australia 2022-12-03 38 3857264 Poland Argentina 2022-11-30 39 3857289 Argentina Mexico 2022-11-26 42 3869519 Argentina Croatia 2022-12-13 56 3857300 Argentina Saudi Arabia 2022-11-22 ``` ::: ::: Match id 3857300 is for the specific game: Argentina vs Saudi Arabia ## Loading the dataframes ::: {#e1bb50b2 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Load match events # https://mplsoccer.readthedocs.io/en/latest/gallery/statsbomb/plot_statsbomb_data.html#event-data events, related, freeze, tactics = parser.event(3857300) # Argentina passes arg_passes = events[ (events['type_name'] == 'Pass') & (events['team_name'] == 'Argentina') ] # Saudi Arabia passes ksa_passes = events[ (events['type_name'] == 'Pass') & (events['team_name'] == 'Saudi Arabia') ] # Argentina shots arg_shots = events[ (events['type_name'] == 'Shot') & (events['sub_type_name'] !='Penalty') & (events['team_name'] == 'Argentina') ] # Saudi Arabia shots ksa_shots = events[ (events['type_name'] == 'Shot') & (events['sub_type_name'] !='Penalty') & (events['team_name'] == 'Saudi Arabia') ] print(f"Argentina passes: {len(arg_passes)}, shots: {len(arg_shots)}") print(f"Saudi Arabia passes: {len(ksa_passes)}, shots: {len(ksa_shots)}") print("* excluding penalties") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Argentina passes: 646, shots: 14 Saudi Arabia passes: 286, shots: 3 * excluding penalties ``` ::: ::: ## Function setup ::: {#cde9e997 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} def get_pre_shot_passes(passes_df, shots_df): """Get passes made within 15 seconds of a shot""" pre_shot = [] # empty list to collect results for _, shot in shots_df.iterrows(): #looping through every shot one at a time shot_time = shot['minute'] * 60 + shot['second'] # converting shot time to total seconds window = passes_df[ (passes_df['minute'] * 60 + passes_df['second']) .between(shot_time - 15, shot_time) #convert every pass time to total seconds # then find passes that happened within the 15 second window BEFORE the shot ] pre_shot.append(window) # add to results list return pd.concat(pre_shot).drop_duplicates() if pre_shot else pd.DataFrame() # combine all results # remove duplicates # return empty dataframe if nothing is found arg_pre_shot = get_pre_shot_passes(arg_passes, arg_shots) ksa_pre_shot = get_pre_shot_passes(ksa_passes, ksa_shots) ``` ::: ## 1. Pass Map Viz - Buildup to the Shot ::: {#fac9724f .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 8)) fig.patch.set_facecolor('#ffffff') fig.suptitle('Pass Buildup to Shot (Within 15 Seconds)', color='black', fontsize=22, y=1.04, fontweight = 'bold') for ax, passes_df, team, color in zip( axes, [arg_pre_shot, ksa_pre_shot], ["Argentina", "Saudi Arabia"], ['#75AADB', '#00b100'] ): pitch = Pitch( pitch_type='statsbomb', pitch_color='#fafafa', line_color='#cccccc', line_zorder=2 ) pitch.draw(ax=ax) # complete passes complete = passes_df[passes_df['outcome_name'].isna()] if not complete.empty: pitch.arrows( complete.x, complete.y, complete.end_x, complete.end_y, ax=ax, color=color, width=2, headwidth=4, alpha=0.8, label='Complete' ) # incomplete passes incomplete = passes_df[passes_df['outcome_name'].notna()] if not incomplete.empty: pitch.arrows( incomplete.x, incomplete.y, incomplete.end_x, incomplete.end_y, ax=ax, color='#000000', width=1.5, headwidth=3, alpha=0.9, label='Incomplete' ) ax.set_title(team, color='black', fontsize=13, pad=10) ax.legend(facecolor='#fafafa', labelcolor='black', loc='upper left', fontsize=13, markerscale=1.5, framealpha=0.8 ) plt.tight_layout() plt.savefig('images/pass_map.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='#fafafa') plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/cell-6-output-1.png){width=1526 height=712} ::: ::: Why Track passes 15 seconds before a shot? This type of tracking reveals the precise off ball movements, spacing and defensive fractures that create scoring opportunities, rather than just analyzing the final action. If the coach only looks at shots, then they're reacting only to the outcome. Looking at passes 15 seconds before a shot can give an idea of spatial patterns before looking at the shot map 🟦 Argentina Takeaways 1. The high volume of passes show that Argentina dominated possession 2. Short and quick arrows are clustered together meaning a lot of tight passing was carried out 3. Argentina controlled the ball and recycled possession heavily in the opponent's half creating a sustained attacking pressure 🟩 Saudi Takeways 1. Saudi Arabia sat deeper, played fewer passes and relied on direct balls when they played forward ## 2. Shot Map ::: {#47f74e0b .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig, axes = plt.subplots(1,2, figsize=(16, 8)) fig.patch.set_facecolor('#ffffff') fig.suptitle('Shot Map', color='black', fontsize=22, y=1.05, fontweight = 'bold') # subtitle fig.text(0.5, 1.00, 'Circle size proportional to xG value', color='#aaaaaa', fontsize=11, ha='center', va='top') for ax, shots_df, team, color in zip( axes, [arg_shots, ksa_shots], ["Argentina", "Saudi Arabia"], ['#75AADB', '#00b100'] ): pitch = Pitch( pitch_type='statsbomb', pitch_color='#fafafa', line_color='#cccccc', half=True ) pitch.draw(ax=ax) # Goals goals = shots_df[shots_df['outcome_name'] == 'Goal'] if not goals.empty: pitch.scatter( goals.x, goals.y, s=goals.shot_statsbomb_xg * 1000, c='#9b00b1', edgecolors='white', linewidth=0.8, ax=ax, zorder=3, label='Goal' ) # Non goals non_goals = shots_df[shots_df['outcome_name'] != 'Goal'] if not non_goals.empty: pitch.scatter( non_goals.x, non_goals.y, s=non_goals.shot_statsbomb_xg * 1000, c=color, edgecolors='white', linewidth=0.8, alpha=0.6, ax=ax, zorder=2, label='No Goal' ) ax.set_title(team, color='black', fontsize=13, pad=10) ax.legend(facecolor='#fafafa', labelcolor='black', loc='upper left', fontsize=13, markerscale=1.5, framealpha=0.8 ) plt.tight_layout() plt.savefig('images/shot_map.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='#fafafa') plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/cell-7-output-1.png){width=1255 height=811} ::: ::: Argentina dominated territorially with 14 shots (excluding the 1 penalty taken by Messi) but Saudi Arabia's disciplined defensive block restricted clear chances. Saudi Arabia took 3 shots to score twice ## 3. Passing Networks ::: {#55cee43d .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Argentina top 5 arg_top5 = arg_passes[ arg_passes['outcome_name'].isna() ].groupby('player_name').size()\ .reset_index(name='total_passes')\ .sort_values('total_passes', ascending=False)\ .head(5) print("Argentina Top 5:") print(arg_top5.to_string()) # Saudi Arabia top 5 ksa_top5 = ksa_passes[ ksa_passes['outcome_name'].isna() ].groupby('player_name').size()\ .reset_index(name='total_passes')\ .sort_values('total_passes', ascending=False)\ .head(5) print("\nSaudi Arabia Top 5:") print(ksa_top5.to_string()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Argentina Top 5: player_name total_passes 11 Nicolás Hernán Otamendi 84 12 Rodrigo Javier De Paul 66 9 Nahuel Molina Lucero 57 1 Cristian Gabriel Romero 55 5 Leandro Daniel Paredes 55 Saudi Arabia Top 5: player_name total_passes 0 Abdulelah Saad Hameed Al-Malki 29 6 Mohammed Kanoo 29 4 Hassan Mohammed Al-Tambakti 22 12 Saud Abdullah Abdul Hamid 21 7 Mohammed Khalil Al Owais 17 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#d2f55c64 .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} def draw_passing_network(ax, passes_df, team, color, top5): """Passing network for top 5 players""" # passes between top 5 players only complete = passes_df[ passes_df['outcome_name'].isna() & passes_df['pass_recipient_name'].notna() & passes_df['player_name'].isin(top5) & passes_df['pass_recipient_name'].isin(top5) ] # pass pairs pairs = complete.groupby( ['player_name', 'pass_recipient_name'] ).size().reset_index(name='pass_count') # average positions avg_pos = complete.groupby('player_name').agg( avg_x=('x', 'mean'), avg_y=('y', 'mean'), total=('x', 'count') ).reset_index() pitch = Pitch( pitch_type='statsbomb', pitch_color='#fafafa', line_color='#cccccc' ) pitch.draw(ax=ax) # draw lines for _, row in pairs.iterrows(): p1 = avg_pos[avg_pos['player_name'] == row['player_name']] p2 = avg_pos[avg_pos['player_name'] == row['pass_recipient_name']] if not p1.empty and not p2.empty: pitch.lines( p1.avg_x.values[0], p1.avg_y.values[0], p2.avg_x.values[0], p2.avg_y.values[0], ax=ax, lw=row['pass_count'] * 0.4, color=color, alpha=0.5, zorder=1 ) # draw nodes pitch.scatter( avg_pos.avg_x, avg_pos.avg_y, s=avg_pos.total * 8, c=color, edgecolors='white', linewidth=1, ax=ax, zorder=3 ) # Labels — last name only texts = [] for _, row in avg_pos.iterrows(): last_name = row['player_name'].split()[-1] txt = ax.text( row['avg_x'], row['avg_y'], last_name, color='black', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='bottom', zorder=5 ) texts.append(txt) # adjustText: avoids label overlap # similar to ggrepel adjust_text( texts, ax=ax, expand=(1.2, 1.4), arrowprops=dict( arrowstyle='-', color='#999999', lw=0.5 ) ) ax.set_title(team, color='black', fontsize=12, pad=12) return ax # top 5 player lists arg_top5_list = arg_top5['player_name'].tolist() ksa_top5_list = ksa_top5['player_name'].tolist() fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(16, 8)) fig.patch.set_facecolor('#fafafa') fig.suptitle('Top 5 Passers', color='black', fontsize=22, fontweight='bold', y=1.04) fig.text( 0.5, 1.00, 'Node size = total passes \n Line width = pass frequency', color='#666666', fontsize=10, fontstyle='italic', ha='center', va='top' ) for ax, passes_df, team, color, top5 in zip( axes, [arg_passes, ksa_passes], ["Argentina", "Saudi Arabia"], ['#75AADB', '#00b100'], [arg_top5_list, ksa_top5_list] ): draw_passing_network(ax, passes_df, team, color, top5) plt.tight_layout() plt.savefig('images/passing_network.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='#fafafa') plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/cell-9-output-1.png){width=475 height=804} ::: ::: Argentina's top 5 passers were almost entirely confined to their own defensive third, a striking visual that tells the story of Saudi Arabia's relentless high press. Otamendi and Romero, both center backs, were forced into heavy ball circulation at the back, with Paredes and De Paul dropping deep to offer passing options rather than driving forward. The tightly clustered network suggests Argentina struggled to progress the ball through midfield and build attacks from deep (an unusual sight for a team of their quality) Saudi Arabia's network tells the opposite story. Their top 5 passers operated across a wider area of the pitch, with Owais distributing from deep while Al-Malki, Kanoo and Hamid formed an active midfield triangle in the center of the pitch
